newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia rejection of START-2 would be costly-Perry.
newsitem.headline: Russia rejection of START-2 would be costly-Perry.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry on Wednesday warned that Russian refusal to approve the START-2 nuclear arms reduction treaty would cost Moscow and Washington billions of dollars and would not delay enlargement of NATO into Eastern Europe.

"Reducing the number of weapons you have by half has to be a cost saver," Perry told reporters who flew to Moscow with him for a visit that will include testimony on Thursday to a hostile Russian parliament in support of the treaty already ratified by the U.S. Senate.

The State Duma lower house of parliament is expected to vote later this year on the treaty. Perry said rejection would cost the United States and cash-strapped Russia billions of dollars more in defence funds to maintain strategic nuclear arms at current levels than to cut Cold War stockpiles under the treaty.

"There are shutdown costs with closing down a missile programme," he conceded in response to hostility in the Duma over slashing U.S. and Russian long-range warheads from 6,000 each to fewer than 3,500 each by the year 2003 under START-2.

"In the United States that (dismantling cost) is measured in several hundreds of millions of dollars. But the savings we estimate from the START treaty are measured in billions of dollars," Perry stressed.

Perry, who was holding talks with Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov later on Wednesday, also said Washington would not allow the Duma to use START-2 as a bargaining chip to keep NATO from extending membership to former Soviet bloc states, expected to initially include Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
